issues.title: Conditional mean incorrectly equated with the argmin set
issues.failure_explanation: For the stated optimization over measurable functions, argmin denotes the set of minimizers, whereas E[Y|X] is a random variable or an L2 equivalence class. Moreover, raw function representatives may differ on P_X-null sets. The proof supports membership in the argmin set and uniqueness only up to P_X-almost-sure equality.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed optimizer statement is literally malformed, but the intended L2 projection and squared-loss decomposition remain valid. No later formal result relies on the erroneous element-to-set equality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the element-to-set equality in eq:cm-opt by a correctly typed statement: a version of the conditional mean belongs to the argmin set, and the minimizer is unique up to P_X-almost-sure equality. Equivalently, identify the unique minimizer in the relevant L2 equivalence-class space. The existing proof and decomposition require no change.
issues.why_classification: The theorem’s projection formulation and eq:det-decomp uniquely force this corrected reading: the excess risk is the squared L2 distance from the conditional mean. The proof never relies on the malformed element-to-set equality, and there is no affected downstream result. This is therefore a directly recoverable notation/type transcription rather than a mathematical argument requiring repair.

issues.title: Undefined explained-variance ratio for zero-variance responses
issues.failure_explanation: Under the active scalar L2 assumptions, Y=c almost surely is admissible. Then Var(Y)=0, so eq:r2 divides by zero, and the normalized identities culminating in eq:r2-ceiling cannot be asserted. The unnormalized squared-loss decomposition and law of total variance remain valid; only their R-squared normalization fails.
issues.overall_effect: The definition of R-squared and its explained-variance ceiling are not well-defined for a constant response. No theorem or proposition is invalidated, and all reported numerical examples have nonzero response variance.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that eq:r2 and all normalized R-squared identities, including eq:r2-ceiling, apply only when Var(Y)>0. Add that when Var(Y)=0, the response is almost surely constant and R-squared is undefined, while the unnormalized squared-loss decomposition and law of total variance remain valid.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine omitted domain qualification, not a transcriptional typo, but adding the standard nonzero-denominator condition is a short and routine local repair. It preserves the method and every regular-case conclusion, does not affect the numerical examples, and has no propagation to a theorem or proposition.

issues.title: Uncorrected threshold in the multi-probe diagnostic figure
issues.failure_explanation: The specified diagnostic tests multiple probes and requires per-probe level alpha divided by the family size. The figure instead uses 1.96, the nominal two-sided 5% single-probe normal cutoff, so its displayed decision boundary does not control the stated family-wise false-positive rate. The reported extrema, approximately 34 and 1.3, remain on the same respective sides of the corrected threshold.
issues.overall_effect: The significance reference line is inconsistent with the controlled diagnostic procedure and would overflag intermediate probes, although the degree-2 and degree-9 regime classifications reported here are unchanged.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the figure’s uncorrected single-probe line |t_n|=1.96 and its caption by the Bonferroni-corrected family-wise 5% cutoff |t_n|=3.15 for the plotted probe family. Recheck the displayed decisions against that line; the reported extrema, approximately 34 and 1.3, remain respectively above and below it, so the two regime classifications are unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The incorrect line is a genuine calibration error in the displayed diagnostic boundary and therefore is not merely typographical. Its correction is nevertheless a routine, local multiple-testing recalculation that leaves the procedure, effect sizes, reported regime classifications, and all downstream conclusions intact.
